intro.title: Four lenses, three axes, one rule
intro.lead: An uncertainty estimator reads an observation from the model's computation and turns it into a score. We build a framework that characterizes uncertainty estimators by the lens they apply, the variables they sample across repeated inferences, and the auxiliary structure they rely on.

figure.title: Four lenses on the residual stream
figure.alt: Figure 3 of the paper. The residual stream of a transformer block, with four lenses along it from inner to outer: the structural lens reads the attention-head and FFN writes, the representational lens reads the hidden state, the distributional lens reads the token distribution after the unembedding, and the semantical lens reads the distribution over meanings given by a relation R. The maps g_sum, g_unemb and g_R link them.
figure.scroll_hint: Scroll sideways to see all of it.

lenses.name: Structural lens
lenses.text: Reads the individual components: each attention-head and FFN write to the residual stream, including the attention weights \(a_c^{(\ell)}\) and the activation \(m^{(\ell)}\).

lenses.name: Representational lens
lenses.text: Reads the hidden state, the residual-stream state that sums the component writes.

lenses.name: Distributional lens
lenses.text: Reads the token distribution, obtained by unembedding the state with \(W_U\).

lenses.name: Semantical lens
lenses.text: Reads the distribution over meanings, obtained with a semantic relation \(R\) between outputs.

maps.discards: Keeps the total update and discards its split among component writes.
Composed of the final normalization, the unembedding \(W_U\), and the softmax. The normalization discards the norm.
Moves the sequence-level prediction onto the meaning space. It discards the lexical form of the outputs and keeps only what \(R\) reads as their meaning, depending on the implementation of \(R\).

axes.title: Every estimator is a point \((\lambda, Z, S)\)

cards.name: lens
cards.title: where it reads
cards.sentence: Which mechanistic object the estimator reads from the residual stream.

cards.name: variation
cards.title: what is resampled
cards.sentence: What varies across forward passes to give several observations.
cards.inference: The LLM \(f_\theta\) maps an input \(x\) to an output \(y\): \(f_\theta(x) = y\).

values.label: one pass
values.definition: No resampling. The estimator reads a single forward pass, and \(\mathcal U\) measures the spread within one atom or across a field.
examples: the entropy of a token distribution [[malinin2021]]

values.label: outputs
values.definition: The output is resampled with \(\theta\) and \(x\) fixed, as in stochastic decoding. \(\mathcal U\) measures the spread across the sampled generations.

values.label: parameters
values.definition: The parameters are resampled from a posterior given the training data \(\mathcal D\), and \(\mathcal U\) measures the spread across models. It is the Bayesian predictive uncertainty.
examples: a fitted approximate posterior \(q(\theta)\) over the weights [[blundell2015]]
a finite ensemble of trained models [[lakshminarayanan2017]]

values.label: inputs
values.definition: The input is resampled, usually within a semantic neighbourhood of \(x\) by paraphrasing or reformulation, and \(\mathcal U\) measures the spread across inputs.

cards.name: auxiliary structure
cards.title: what extra structure is used
cards.sentence: The auxiliary axis \(S\) covers the structure an estimator needs beyond the observation \(O_\lambda\) and the variation \(Z\).

pipeline.title: How the parts compose (select a box)

boxes.label: \(O_\lambda\)
boxes.definition: What the lens reads from the residual stream: component writes, the hidden state, the token distribution, or the distribution over meanings.

boxes.label: \(\rho_S\)
boxes.definition: A readout map that transforms each observation before scoring.

boxes.label: \(\{\,\cdot\,\}_{Z\sim Z_S}\)
boxes.label_text: collect over Z drawn from Z S
boxes.definition: Resample \(Z\) across forward passes to collect several observations. \(S\) defines the distribution \(Z_S\) it is drawn from.

boxes.label: \(\mathcal U_S\)
boxes.definition: \(\mathcal U\) measures the spread of the observations and returns a scalar. When \(S\) parameterizes it, \(\mathcal U\) is an external model \(\mathcal U_S\), trained against a target.
examples: a trained linear probe on hidden states [[azaria2023]]
a Dirichlet head over the token distribution [[malinin2021]]
boxes.default: \(\mathcal U\) a fixed function, e.g. the entropy of a token distribution [[malinin2021]]

boxes.label: \(\psi_S\)
boxes.definition: A lens-agnostic step applied to the score after \(\mathcal U_S\).
examples: conformal prediction, which uses a calibration set to give coverage guarantees [[quach2024]]

boxes.label: \(U_\lambda(x)\)
boxes.definition: A scalar that predicts how uncertain the LLM is about its response.

pipeline.defaults_html: The default \(Z=\varnothing\), \(\rho_S = I\), \(\mathcal U_S\) fixed and \(\psi_S\) the identity is the fixed single-pass estimator.

rule.title: Choosing a lens and an estimator on it
rule.text_html: Pick the lens that is sufficient for the target, then choose \(Z\) and \(S\) for efficiency.

glosses.text: For a target, consider the outermost lens \(\lambda^*\) that is sufficient for it. Any lens \(\lambda \succeq \lambda^*\) can be read to recover the target (Permission). No estimator that reads only a lens further out can recover it (Prohibition).
Among the estimators that read a sufficient lens, the choice comes down to efficiency, which is set by the variation \(Z\) and the auxiliary structure \(S\).

tieback.title: Choosing the lens for the four examples

rows.why: The samples agree on a wrong answer, but only the hidden state shows doubt.
The token spread is mostly wording, while most answers share one stance.
The output says Lyon, but only the component writes show which parts pull toward the context and which toward memory.
One pass of the token distribution already shows the split, whereas grouping by meaning needs 20 samples.

takeaways.title: Communication channel in transformers
takeaways.body_html: All communication in a transformer is mediated by the residual stream, since every component at every layer and position reads from and writes to it. [[elhage2021]]

takeaways.title: Definition of mechanistic observation lenses
takeaways.body_html: The mechanistic observation lenses are identified by the mechanistic object they read from the residual stream. From innermost to outermost, the structural lens reads the component updates; the representational lens reads the hidden state; the distributional lens reads the token distribution; and the semantical lens reads the distribution over meanings induced by a semantic relation \(R\) between outputs.

takeaways.title: Characterizing an uncertainty estimator
takeaways.body_html: An uncertainty estimator is characterized by the lens \(\lambda\) it reads, the variation \(Z\) it resamples, and the auxiliary structure \(S\) it uses. The lens is set by the mechanistic object the estimator reads. The variation changes which observations are collected and the auxiliary structure changes how they are scored, but neither changes the lens. An estimator is native if it estimates the uncertainty of the lens it reads, and surrogate if it estimates the uncertainty of another lens.

takeaways.title: Choosing a lens by sufficiency and efficiency
takeaways.body_html: The four lenses are ordered by the information they carry, and each outer lens discards some information from the adjacent inner lens. For an uncertainty target, whether the target depends on the discarded information determines the sufficiency of the lens, and what variable is resampled and what auxiliary structure is used determine the efficiency of the estimator. The suited lens is sufficient for the target and admits an efficient estimator.
